text: Valis — build exercise (Principal, GTM)
**The setup.** You've been dropped in next to **Dana Whitfield, CEO of Northwind Media** — a
~300-person creator-economy company. Her data is scattered across Slack, spreadsheets, meeting notes,
and an org chart, and — her words — she's *"drowning in dashboards and doesn't fully trust her own
numbers."* You have **one focused day** to show what a Valis-style first slice looks like — **built by
hand, on her real (synthetic) mess.**
Everything in this folder is **100% synthetic** — a fabricated company. Use it freely; nothing here is
real client data.
**Start with `CEO_CONTEXT.md`** (Dana's framing), then **`CEO_QUESTIONS.md`** (what she's asking). The
rest is the raw material to work from.
What's attached — the "Northwind-in-a-box" bundle
- `CEO_CONTEXT.md` — Dana's orientation note · **read first**
- `CEO_QUESTIONS.md` — the questions to answer
- `org_chart.md` — leadership and team structure
- `pnl_q1_2026.csv` — quarterly P&L extract
- `headcount_roster.csv` — headcount roster + open requisitions (snapshot 2026-05-01)
- `support_tickets_q1_2026.csv` — support-ticket log
- `slack_export.md` — `#leadership` / `#finance` / `#ops` / `#people`, ~8 weeks
- `meeting_notes/` — leadership sync, finance review, data review

How to work it
- **Time-box.** One focused day (~8h). Solo. **Use your own AI tooling — Claude, MCP, skills — heavily;
we want to see you AI-native.** The test is whether *you* drive, debug, and own the output, not
whether your agent can.
- **How to submit.** Send back one folder (your artifact + build log + value-number worksheet + builder
spec). Then we'll do a **30-minute live walkthrough** where you screen-share, reproduce a step or two
we pick on the spot — possibly on a fresh file you haven't seen — and we'll push on the value number.
- **What "show your work" means here.** Every number traces to a row. Confidence is honest — high where
the data is clean, *"I couldn't verify this"* where it isn't. If a question has no clean answer in the
data, say so and tell us what you'd need — **don't manufacture one.** The right answer matters less
than that it's true and traceable.
*Valis — confidential. Shared under NDA.*
A note from Dana
Hi — thanks for jumping in.

I'm Dana Whitfield, CEO of Northwind Media. We're about 300 people in the creator economy: we manage and grow online creators, sell brand partnerships, produce a lot of content, and we've got a small product and data team holding the tooling together. We've grown fast, which is great, and also means a lot of how we run is still held together with spreadsheets, Slack threads, and the heroics of a few people who "just know how it works."

Here's my honest #1 frustration: **I'm drowning in dashboards and status meetings, and I don't fully trust my own numbers.** Every team has its own view of the truth, the same metric means three different things depending on who you ask, and by the time something reaches me it's been summarized so many times I can't tell what's a fact and what's a vibe. I don't want more dashboards. I want someone who can go into the raw stuff, reconcile it, and tell me straight what's actually true — and where it isn't, say so instead of papering over it.

**What's in this folder:** I've dropped in a slice of how we actually operate — last quarter's financials (the P&L and a few supporting exports), a headcount roster, support ticket data, and a pile of Slack and meeting notes from the last couple of months. It's deliberately messy, just like real life. There's a short `CEO_QUESTIONS.md` with the two things I most want answered plus a question about where we're wasting time. Dig into the source files, cross-check them against each other, and give me answers you'd be willing to stake your name on. If two sources disagree, I'd rather hear "these don't reconcile and here's why" than a clean number that's wrong.
Thanks — looking forward to seeing how you think.
— Dana
Questions for the Operator

A few things I want a clear read on. Dig into the data we've got — the P&L export, the headcount roster, the Slack threads, the meeting notes, the support tickets — and come back with straight answers.
— Dana Whitfield, CEO
Q1. SaaS spend
**"What did we actually spend on SaaS tools last quarter?"**
I want the real number for software/SaaS for Q1 2026. Finance has the P&L line items; pull it from there and tell me what we're paying for.
Q2. Sales hiring
**"Did we decide to hire in Sales or freeze hiring — what's the current state, and who owns it?"**
There's been back-and-forth on this. I need to know where we landed, what the situation is right now, and who's accountable for the call.
Workflow
**"Where are we wasting the most time, and what would you automate first?"**
Across the company — ops, finance, content, support — where is manual effort piling up? If you could automate one workflow, what would it be and why?
*Use whatever sources you need. I care more about a correct, well-supported answer than a fast one.*
